# The Iron Arteries of the Alps: A History of Alpine Railways in Engineering, Tourism, and Politics

## I. The Mountain as Problem and Promise

The Alps do not yield to the flat logic of the railway. Where the engineer of the English or Saxon plain could unroll a line of iron track across gentle undulations, the alpine builder confronted a geography that seemed to make mechanized transit a proposition for the mad. The mountains rise in sheer limestone walls, fracture into gorges a thousand meters deep, crown their summits with perpetual snow, and shift their bedsides in the spring thaw. To drive a railway through them was, in the mid-nineteenth century, to attempt what many considered physically impossible.
